title: George Carlin   Shell Shock
summary: A short George Carlin routine on how the term shell shock was softened into combat fatigue and then PTSD. He argues that euphemism hides the reality of suffering.
why: It is cited in debates about euphemism and language policing, usually by commenters who think softer terms change nothing.

quote.text: I’ll betcha, if we’da still been calling it ‘Shell Shock,’ some of those Vietnam veterans might have gotten the attention they needed at the time.
